sections.title: Why a backend developer needs this

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: Your PDFs do not cover this topic, so this page was written for the site. Your 12-week plan lists React, hooks, rendering, performance, state management and TypeScript. Check it against the official documentation, or give me a PDF to replace it.

blocks: A React component ends up as HTML and CSS in the browser. You do not need to be a designer, but you need to read and write semantic markup, build forms that work, and lay out a page with Flexbox and Grid.

sections.title: Semantic HTML and forms
blocks: Choose elements for their meaning, not their looks. `button` is focusable and keyboard-operable for free; a clickable `div` is neither. Screen readers and search engines rely on `header`, `nav`, `main`, `section`, `article` and heading levels.

blocks.code:
<form action="/api/login" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required autocomplete="username" />

  <label for="password">Password</label>
  <input id="password" name="password" type="password" required minlength="8" />

  <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
</form>
blocks.title: A form that works before any JavaScript

blocks: `label for` links the label to the input, which also makes the label clickable. Browser validation (`required`, `type="email"`) is a convenience for the user only: **the server must validate again**, because anyone can send a request without your form.

sections.title: The box model
blocks: Every element is a box: content, then padding, then border, then margin. By default `width` sets the content only, so padding makes the box wider than you asked for. Almost every project starts with `box-sizing: border-box`, which makes `width` include padding and border.

rows: One: a row or a column
Toolbars, nav bars, centring, lists of chips

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: A selector's specificity decides which rule wins, not just its order. `#id` beats `.class` beats `element`. Reaching for `!important` usually means a specificity problem.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Use semantic elements: `button` for actions, `a` for navigation, `label` for every input.
- Browser validation helps the user; only the server's validation protects you.
- Set `box-sizing: border-box` globally.
- Flexbox for one direction, Grid for two.

items.question: Why is a `button` better than a clickable `div`?
items.answer: It is focusable, works with Enter and Space, and is announced as a button by screen readers, all without extra code.

items.question: What does `box-sizing: border-box` change?
items.answer: `width` and `height` include padding and border, so adding padding does not make the box bigger.

items.question: You need a responsive card gallery. Flexbox or Grid?
items.answer: Grid, with `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr))`: it is a two-dimensional layout and needs no media queries.
